evals.prompt: I'm starting a URL shortener service in this empty directory and want to track its requirements with SLCR (the `slcr` CLI is installed). Set it up and write the requirements: POST /links creates a short link and returns its code; GET /{code} redirects with a 301; codes are exactly 7 base62 characters; users may optionally pick a custom alias; every request must be authenticated with either an API key or an OAuth token. Make sure it's valid and render the markdown.
evals.expected_output: SLCR.toml and a spec created via slcr init, requirements with explicit refines/refinement (auth as OR over MAY children), modality keywords in bodies, slcr vet clean, SPEC.md rendered.

evals.prompt: This repo specifies a todo API in SLCR (SPEC.slcr.toml). Add a requirement that the endpoint accepts DELETE to remove an item, and that deleting also requires the request to be authenticated like POST and GET do. Give it an acceptance criterion too. Keep everything valid.
evals.expected_output: New REQ-011 under REQ-001 refining it; REQ-004's refines gains REQ-011 (not a duplicate auth requirement); DELETE has refinement AND; AC-002 added; no IDs renumbered; vet clean.

evals.prompt: In this shop project, REQ-002 (cart total) isn't proven by anything yet. src/cart.sh is the implementation. Add whatever's needed so `slcr check` proves it, and tell me the status of every requirement afterward.
evals.expected_output: A .validators.slcr.* file referencing shop/REQ-002 with tool sh and a script that can fail; manifest pin untouched; slcr check run; honest report that REQ-002 is satisfied and others unknown / coverage gaps.
